label: Jupiter approach in color
why: A month of color pictures as Cassini closed on Jupiter, the time-lapse of its bands and the Great Red Spot turning

label: Phoebe up close
why: The first close look at a moon in the Saturn system: a captured, cratered remnant of the outer Solar System, three weeks before arrival

label: Huygens descends to Titan
why: Released by Cassini on Christmas Day 2004, Huygens parachutes through Titan's haze, its camera mapping rivers and shorelines down to the surface

label: Hyperion, the sponge moon
why: The only close flyby of tumbling Hyperion, its deep sponge-like craters lit at a low Sun

label: Dione up close
why: The first close flyby of Dione: bright ice cliffs and cratered plains from 500 km

label: Iapetus up close
why: The only close flyby of two-toned Iapetus: its dark leading side, bright trailing side and the great equatorial ridge

label: Enceladus's plumes
why: Backlit by the Sun, the jets from Enceladus's south pole fan out into space: the plumes of an ocean moon

label: Mimas and its giant crater
why: The closest flyby of Mimas, the 'Death Star' moon, sweeping over the great crater Herschel

label: Rhea up close
why: Four hours of a close Rhea flyby, its bright wispy fractures and old cratered plains

label: The Great Northern Storm
why: Almost a day of color movie frames of the northern hemisphere as the great storm of 2010-2011 wraps around the planet

label: Epimetheus up close
why: The best look at Epimetheus, the moon that swaps orbits with Janus every four years
